title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 84
paragraphs: The Argives, then, say that this is why Cleomenes went mad and came to a bad end. The Spartans themselves, however, say that Cleomenes was not driven mad by any divine power. He had taken, they say, to drinking wine unmixed with water, a habit he picked up from keeping company with Scythians, and that is what made him mad. The nomadic Scythians, after Darius had invaded their country, were eager to take revenge on him, and sent to Sparta proposing an alliance: the Scythians were to invade Media by way of the river Phasis, while the Spartans were to march up inland from Ephesus, and the two forces would meet at an appointed place. The Spartans say that when the Scythians arrived on this business, Cleomenes spent a great deal of time with them — too much, in fact — and that by this association he learned to drink wine unmixed; and this, as the Spartans believe, is what drove him mad. Ever since then, when they want to drink stronger wine, they say “Fill it up, Scythian style.” That is what the Spartans say about Cleomenes. To me, though, it seems that his fate was the retribution he paid for Demaratus.
